original_dispositions.title: The latency harness reads open inputs and root state by key, with backoff, not by 2 ms full listing
The per-commit session graph cache and derived read view update incrementally, not by full rebuild
Live replay retention does not keep a full read view per retained event
The 1-lane CPU and RSS growth per turn is attributed to named sites
A session queues at most one pending drive invocation
A root's scope close is written in its terminal commit, not as a separate step after it
SQLite WAL checkpoints keep up under concurrent lanes
Open-input scans use the state index, so their cost does not grow with session history
LashTurn records turn config and environment sync as one prelude step
A cross-worker follower learns its root's terminal from one open wait, not a store poll plus a capped read
A turn journals a request digest instead of the full transcript twice, with fewer recorded steps
The turn's report is handed to its waiter at TurnPersisted, before the post-commit tail
Turn cancel gates and settlement do not make nested index invocations
The per-session durable-wait index keeps bounded state and loads it lazily
The follower resolves its root with point reads, never the applications scan
SQLite writers queue on an in-process FIFO gate instead of sleeping in busy_timeout, and statements are cached
The latency gate's harness measures without rescanning session history
A recovering deployment retakes a claim as soon as its holder is known dead, not only after the claim TTL
